affected_boundaries: Git mutation outside transaction and integrated-file assessment under database lock

observed_behavior: Certificate assessment accepted and published its checkpoint while another increment retained PUSHING ownership of the coordinator integration lane.
expected_behavior: Integrated inputs remain stable during certificate assessment; in-flight Git integration must finish before assessment can begin.
causal_mechanism: The project database lock serialized mutations, but publication commits its push intent before mutating Git outside that transaction. Assessment checked only its already-published increment and could overlap a newer integration using the same checkout.

anti_pattern.structural_description: Treating a database transaction as protection for external mutations whose intents have already committed.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: The external Git operation can change assessed inputs after validation and before certificate publication.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: No active integration may own the same coordinator checkout when assessment enters its serialized critical section.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: Within the existing project transaction, refuse assessment while any project campaign with that canonical coordinator root has an active unrepaired increment. The same project lock prevents a new intent being claimed until assessment finishes.

applicability_conditions: External Git mutation follows a committed database intent.
Multiple increments can become ready while a published increment awaits certificate assessment.
known_non_matches: Already published receipts and conflicts returned to worker repair do not own an active integration lane.
confirmation_evidence: The focused regression reported Missing expected rejection when a valid active PUSHING row was present.
Adding the lane fence makes the full assessment Arc pass and verifies the accepted file remains unchanged during refusal.
regression_proofs: tests/rolling-campaign-store.integration.test.ts: integrated certificate assessment uses retained published proof and serializes accepted record publication
